title: Man dies in police custody
article: An investigation into the death of prisoner while in police custody is in the hands of provincial investigators.

Special Investigations Unit (SIU) spokesman John Yoannou said investigators are examining details surrounding the death of 36-year-old Port Hope resident Darryl Thompson. Mr. Thompson was found absent of vital signs in his cell during a cell check at 11 a.m. Wednesday morning, said Mr. Yoannou. EMS attended the scene and transported the man to Northumberland Hills Hospital where he was pronounced dead. An autopsy completed Thursday did not determine the cause of Mr. Thompson's death and toxicology tests have been ordered, he said.
The SIU is called in the investigate when a death or serious injury occurs involving police.

The SIU spokesman said a woman was walking her dog in the area of 76 Cavan Street at 12:20 a.m. on Aug. 20, and spotted a man lying unconscious on the front lawn. The man living inside one of the homes called the Port Hope Police Service, he said. Officers arrested and charged the man with public intoxication, transported him back to the station and placed him in a cell.

Four SIU investigators (two field and two forensic) have been assigned to the case, said Mr. Yoannou. The investigators are interviewing three officers - two officers directly involved in the arrest process and another as a witness. Under SIU protocol, the names of the officers under interview are not released unless charges are filed in connection with an incident, he explained.
PHPS Chief Ron Hoath said there was nothing to add to the SIU information and noted all comments about the incident must come through the SIU.

At the July 10 Port Hope Police Services Board (PHPSB) meeting, Chief Hoath provided a written report that stated the current PHPS building does not meet provincial standards - notably in the cell area. The report, forwarded to Port Hope council, advised the elected officials to immediately move ahead with a new building. He also requested council provide a written disclaimer to absolve PHPSB members, the police chief and all officers of any liability arising from building deficiencies recognized as below standard.There is extreme liability in the event of a cell death and the onus must be placed on council since it is responsible for adequate funding under the provincial Police Services Act, stated the chief.
It is not known if Mr. Thompson's death is related to the chief's concerns about the cells.

The SIU is looking for the public's assistance into Mr. Thompson's death. They are asking anyone who was with Mr. Thompson prior to his being found on the Cavan Street lawn to make contact with police.
In particular, investigators are looking for the woman who was walking her dog at the scene.
